Job offer review and negotiation service for six-figure professionals
6.3
/10

THE IDEA

A senior product manager gets an offer at 5pm on a Thursday: $185K base, RSUs, a signing bonus, and 48 hours to sign. She has done 20 interview rounds over two months (up 42% from 2021), she has watched 176,800 tech workers get laid off this year, and the recruiter has already told her the number is 'final.' She has one night to decide if this is a career move or a trap. Her options: pay Levels.fyi $660 to $1,887 and wait a week, pay Josh Doody $4,000 plus 10% of the increase, or open ChatGPT and hope for the best. 63% of professionals used AI for negotiation this year, and buyers on Blind still ask, every week, if there is someone real they can pay.

This is a 48-hour job offer review for $100K+ professionals. You send the offer, the recruiter's emails, and a link to the company. An AI agent builds an Employer Risk Report (layoffs, funding, exec turnover, reposted listings, Glassdoor patterns) inside 10 minutes. A human coach spends 45 minutes on video with you, walks you through the counter script, the questions to ask the hiring manager, and the contract clauses that matter. You get a written verdict inside 48 hours. Price: $299 flat plus 15% of any comp increase, capped at year one, refund if the increase is under $5K.

WHY NOW

Companies run 42% more interview rounds, then give 48 hours to decide

Three shifts converged in 2026 to make the offer decision the highest-stakes moment of the job search. First, the interview process got longer, not shorter. SHRM's 2026 benchmark of 4,657 recruiters puts overall time-to-fill at about 44 days, and companies now run 20 interviews per hire on average, up from 14 in 2021, a 42 percent rise. A candidate who sits through six rounds over two months arrives at the offer emotionally spent and unwilling to walk away, which is exactly the moment a coach earns their fee.

Second, exploding offer deadlines have crossed over from consulting and finance into tech and VC-backed startups. Recruiters in 2026 report 24 to 72 hour windows are now standard for competitive offers, and INSEAD research shows these tight windows cut job-match quality by 8 to 13 percent. The candidate does not have two weeks to think; they have two nights. A same-day dossier is the only product that fits that clock.

WHO YOU'RE UP AGAINST

7 PLAYERS

Levels.fyi

INCUMBENT

Runs the biggest branded salary negotiation service in tech: pairs candidates with ex-recruiters, promises minimum increase or money back, and claims $100M+ negotiated in increases across thousands of offers.

Rora

(formerly Moonchaser) charges a percentage of the offer increase, not a flat fee, and pays out only if candidate accepts.

Fearless Salary Negotiation

(Josh Doody) is the single-founder premium option: $4,000 strategy fee plus 10 percent of first-year salary increase.

Candor

Runs a done-with-you negotiation service on a pure success fee: candidate pays a percentage of the offer increase, nothing if no improvement or if they do not join.

The Salary Negotiator

(Brandon Bramley, solo operator) charges a $2,250 fixed fee, promises a $10,000 minimum increase or refund, and gates the service to candidates earning $130,000 or more per year.

IGotAnOffer

A marketplace with 300+ coaches (many ex-FAANG) offering hourly interview, resume, and salary negotiation coaching.

Final Round AI

Free ChatGPT / Claude workflows plus Levels.fyi's free compensation database are the true default alternative in 2026.

THE VERDICT

Should you build this?

REASONS TO BUILD

Buyers already pay $1K to $6K for this on Blind, one reported his spouse got $25K-$30K more from a $1K Levels.fyi coach, so the willingness to pay is proven and the $299 price is a genuine wedge under the incumbent.
The gap is real: Levels.fyi charges $660 to $1,887 and takes weeks, Josh Doody starts at $4K, Rora and Candor are executive-only or referral-only, and nobody ships a 48-hour turnaround for the $120K-$180K product/sales/ops buyer who is the fat middle of the market.
The distribution wedge is unusually clean: candidates already post their offers in Blind and r/cscareerquestions threads asking 'is this company safe,' so a free AI-generated Employer Risk Report drops straight into the pain moment at sub-$1 API cost per lead.
An AI-leveraged solo founder can actually deliver the dossier, the counter script, and the 48-hour SLA that human coaches physically cannot match, which flips the incumbent's biggest weakness (speed) into your only real feature.

REASONS TO NOT BUILD

Search volume for the packaged service is thin: 170/mo for 'salary negotiation coach,' 20/mo for 'salary negotiation service,' 0/mo for 'job offer review service.' You will not grow this with SEO or paid ads; you have to hand-place yourself in every Blind thread for the first year.
Free ChatGPT plus Levels.fyi's free comp database is the real competitor, and 63% of professionals in a 2026 survey said AI already helped them get a better offer. The $299 buyer has to believe your dossier beats what they can get for free in 20 minutes.
Success-fee enforcement at $299 AOV is messy: buyer signs, ghosts, disputes the 15% on their card, and a solo founder eats the leakage. Expect 20-30% of success fees to vanish in year one before you build the paper trail Rora and Candor rely on.
Trust cliff is brutal without an ex-FAANG-recruiter name on the landing page. Levels.fyi says $100M negotiated, Josh Doody has ten years of testimonials, and a no-name generalist gets ignored at any price.
